(3.3.26)

Here,
(\psi_{\mathcal{G}},f)\colon(\mathcal{G}^{\prime}_{1}\rightrightarrows M^{\prime})\rightarrow(\mathcal{G}_{1}\rightrightarrows M)
and

(\psi_{\mathcal{H}},f)\colon(\mathcal{H}^{\prime}_{1}\rightrightarrows M^{\prime})\rightarrow(\mathcal{H}_{1}\rightrightarrows M)
are Morita morphisms of Lie groupoids. Then, by
Proposition

3.3.4

B\mathcal{G}^{\prime}\cong B\mathcal{G}
and
B\mathcal{H}^{\prime}\cong B\mathcal{H}
, and commutativity of
Equation

3.3.26
gives the following commutative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{G}^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{H}^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{H}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

Reorganizing the above diagram we obtain,

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{G}^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{H}^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B\mathcal{H}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi}

Thus, the gerbe
\Phi\colon B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
is isomorphic to the gerbe
\Phi^{\prime}\colon B\mathcal{G}^{\prime}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}^{\prime}
. Repeating the same argument for a Morita morphism from the Lie groupoid extension
\phi^{\prime}\colon\mathcal{G}^{\prime}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}^{\prime}_{1}\rightrightarrows M^{\prime}
to
\phi^{\prime\prime}\colon\mathcal{G}^{\prime\prime}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}^{\prime\prime}_{1}\rightrightarrows M^{\prime\prime}
, we complete the proof.

∎

Remark 3.3.11
.

Let
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
be a gerbe over a stack. Assume further that
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\times_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{D}
is a representable surjective submersion. In particular, this means there exists atlases
\underline{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
and
\underline{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}
respectively for the stacks
\mathcal{C}
and
\mathcal{D}
such that the smooth map
X\times_{\mathcal{D}}X\rightarrow X\times_{\mathcal{C}}X
is a surjective submersion (
Remark

3.2.9
).
Now we make the following observation:

Let
(\Phi,1_{M}):(\mathcal{G}_{1}\rightrightarrows M)\rightarrow(\mathcal{H}_{1}\rightrightarrows M)
be a Lie groupoid extension and

B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
be the associated morphism of stacks. Then

1.

the morphism of stacks
B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
is a gerbe over the stack
B\mathcal{H}
(
Theorem

3.3.10
).

2.

there exists atlases
\underline{M}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
and
\underline{M}\rightarrow B\mathcal{G}
satisfying
\underline{M}\times_{B\mathcal{G}}\underline{M}=\mathcal{G}_{1}
and
\underline{M}\times_{B\mathcal{H}}\underline{M}=\mathcal{H}_{1}
. Moreover, the smooth map
\Phi:\mathcal{G}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{1}
associated to the morphism of stacks
\underline{M}\times_{B\mathcal{G}}\underline{M}\rightarrow\underline{M}\times_{B\mathcal{H}}\underline{M}
is a surjective submersion.

Chapter 4
Chern-Weil theory for principal bundles over Lie groupoids

Let
G
be a Lie group,
M
a smooth manifold, and
P(M,G)
a principal bundle. In
Section

2.4
, we have given the construction of Atiyah sequence for
P(M,G)
. Then, we introduced the notion of connection (and curvature) for
P(M,G)
using the Atiyah sequence. We have also mentioned the Chern-Weil map associated to the principal bundle
P(M,G)
. In this chapter, which is based on our paper
[
9
]
, we have introduced the notion of Atiyah sequence and the Chern-Weil map for a principal bundle over Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

4.1
Principal bundle over Lie groupoids

In this section we recall the notion of principal bundle over Lie groupoid. This notion of principal bundle over Lie groupoid can be found in
[
40
,
11
,
48
,
66
]
.

Definition 4.1.1
.

Let
G
be a Lie group, and
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
a Lie groupoid. A
principal
G
-bundle over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
consists of the following data:

1.

a principal
G
-bundle
\pi:E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
over the manifold
X_{0}
,

2.

a smooth map
\mu:X_{1}\times_{s,X_{0},\pi}E_{G}\rightarrow E_{G}
giving an action
(\pi,\mu)
of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on the manifold
E_{G}
,

such that
(\gamma\cdot a)g=\gamma\cdot(ag)
for each
(\gamma,a,g)\in X_{1}\times_{s,X_{0},\pi}E_{G}\times G
.

We denote a principal
G
-bundle over a Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
as

(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

A principal
G
-bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])

gives a natural Lie groupoid structure on
[s^{*}E_{G}:=X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
with source, target maps respectively being
(\gamma,a)\mapsto a
and
(\gamma,a)\mapsto\gamma a
, and composition
\big((\gamma,a),(\gamma^{\prime},b)\big)\mapsto(\gamma^{\prime}\circ\gamma,a)
.

This notion of a principal
G
-bundle over a Lie groupoid includes several classical cases of principal bundles, such as a principal bundle over a manifold, an equivariant principal bundle.

Example 4.1.2
.

Let
H
be a Lie group, and
[H\rightrightarrows*]
the associated Lie groupoid. Let
G
be a Lie group.
A principal
G
-bundle over
[H\rightrightarrows*]
is the same as a
left action of the Lie group
H
on the manifold
G
that commutes with the right translation action of
G
on itself.

Example 4.1.3
.

For a smooth manifold
M
, a Lie group
G
, a principal
G
-bundle over
M
is a principal
G
-bundle over the Lie groupoid
[M\rightrightarrows M]
.

Example 4.1.4
.

Let
M
be a smooth manifold and
G,H
are Lie groups acting on
M
. Consider the Lie groupoid
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
, associated to the action of
H
on
M
. A principal
G
-bundle over
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
is given by a principal
G
-bundle over the manifold
M
, with an action of the Lie groupoid
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
on
P
. This action of
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
gives an action of
H
on the manifold
P
. The compatibility condition between the actions of
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
and
G
on
P
means that the actions of
G,H
on
P
are compatible and that the map
\pi:P\rightarrow M
is
H
-equivariant. Thus, we have a
H
-equivariant principal
G
-bundle
\pi:P\rightarrow M
. So, a principal
G
-bundle over
[H\times M\rightrightarrows M]
is precisely a
H
-equivariant principal
G
-bundle over
M
.

Definition 4.1.5
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. A
morphism of principal bundles from
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
to
(E_{G}^{\prime}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
is given by a morphism
\psi:E_{G}\rightarrow E_{G}^{\prime}
of principal bundles over the manifold
X_{0}
, such that, the following diagram is commutative,

As mentioned in the introduction of this chapter, given a principal bundle
P(M,G)
, we have the short exact sequence of vector bundles over the manifold
M
(Diagram
2.4.6
). Using similar ideas, we construct a short exact sequence of vector bundles over the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, for a principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
. For this, firstly, we recall the notion of a vector bundle over a Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Definition 4.1.6

(
[
48
, Section
5.4
]
)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. A
vector bundle over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
consists of the following data:

1.

a vector bundle
E\rightarrow X_{0}
over the manifold
X_{0}
,

2.

a smooth map
\mu:X_{1}\times_{s,X_{0},\pi}E\rightarrow E
giving an action
(\pi,\mu)
of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on the manifold
E
,

such that, for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
, the map
\mu(\gamma,-):E_{s(\gamma)}\rightarrow E_{t(\gamma)}
is a linear map.

Definition 4.1.7
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. A
morphism of vector bundles from
(E\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
to
(E^{\prime}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
is given by a morphism
\psi:E\rightarrow E^{\prime}
of vector bundles over the manifold
X_{0}
, such that the following diagram commutes,

For a Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, the tangent bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
does not always have a canonical structure of a vector bundle over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. We need an extra structure on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, the notion of a connection, which we define below.

Consider the vector bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
. For it to be a vector bundle over the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we need an action of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on the manifold
TX_{0}
; that is a smooth map
\mu:X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}TX_{0}\rightarrow TX_{0}
. As mentioned before, this would assign a map
\mu(\gamma,-):T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
. This should remind the notion of a connection on the vector bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
, that assigns a linear map
T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
for each path
s(\gamma)\rightarrow t(\gamma)
in
X_{0}
. The case
\mu:X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}TX_{0}\rightarrow TX_{0}
is not exactly similar, but we would still call it “a connection”, on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

We introduce a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
as a sub bundle
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
, that complements the kernel of the differential
s_{*}
, and satisfies certain compatibility conditions related to the other structure maps of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. To specify the compatibility with the structure maps, we would have to see it as a data that assigns
T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
.

Definition 4.1.8
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. A sub bundle
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is said to be
complementing the kernel of
s_{*}
, if, for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
, we have

T_{\gamma}X_{1}=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\oplus\ker(s_{*,\gamma}).

Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a sub bundle complementing the kernel of
s_{*}
. Let
\gamma\in X_{1}
. Consider the map
s_{*,\gamma}:T_{\gamma}X_{1}\rightarrow T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}
. As
s_{*,\gamma}
is a surjective map, the restriction of
s_{*,\gamma}
to the complement of
\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
is an isomorphism; that is,

s_{*,\gamma}|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\rightarrow T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}
is an isomorphism.

Consider the composition
T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
of the maps
s^{-1}_{*,\gamma}|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}}
, and

t_{*,\gamma}
. For our convenience, we denote this composition as
\theta_{\gamma}
. Now we are in a position to define the notion of a connection on a Lie groupoid as a sub bundle satisfying certain conditions.

Definition 4.1.9

(
[
11
, Definition
3.1.
]
)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. A
connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
is a sub bundle
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
, that complements the kernel of
s_{*}
, such that, the following conditions holds:

1.

\theta_{\gamma\circ\gamma^{\prime}}=\theta_{\gamma}\circ\theta_{\gamma^{\prime}}
for each
(\gamma,\gamma^{\prime})\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}X_{1}
,

2.

e_{*,a}(T_{a}X_{0})=\mathcal{H}_{1_{a}}
for all
a\in X_{0}
.

Observe that, to construct
\theta_{\gamma}
, we have used the target map. The first condition in
Definition

4.1.9
is about the compatibility of the choice of
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
, with the composition map
m:X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}X_{1}\rightarrow X_{1}
, and the second condition is about the compatibility with the identity map
e:X_{0}\rightarrow X_{1}
. We have not mentioned about the compatibility with the inverse map
i:X_{1}\rightarrow X_{1}
, because, it follows from the above conditions that,
i_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1})=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma^{-1}}X_{1}
for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
.

Now we give some examples of connections on Lie groupoids.

Example 4.1.10
.

Let
[M\rightrightarrows M]
be the Lie groupoid associated to a manifold
M
. The source map is the identity map. So,
\ker(s_{*,\gamma})=\{0\}
for each
\gamma\in M
. The assignment
\gamma\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}M=T_{\gamma}M
for
\gamma\in M
defines a connection on the Lie groupoid
[M\rightrightarrows M]
.

Example 4.1.11
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be an ètale Lie groupoid. As the source map is a local diffeomorphism, we have
\ker(s_{*,\gamma})=\{0\}
for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
. The assignment
\gamma\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}=T_{\gamma}X_{1}
for
\gamma\in X_{1}
defines a connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Example 4.1.12
.

Consider the Lie groupoid
[M\times G\rightrightarrows M]
associated to an action of a Lie group
G
on a manifold
M
. In this case, the source map is the projection map. So,
\ker(s_{*,(m,g)})=\{0\}\times T_{g}G
for each
(m,g)\in M\times G
. The assignment
(m,g)\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{(m,g)}(M\times G)=T_{m}M
for
(m,g)\in M\times G
defines a connection on the Lie groupoid
[M\times G\rightrightarrows M]
.

Remark 4.1.13

(Notation)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Let
\gamma\in X_{1}
. We have the decomposition
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\oplus\ker(s_{*,\gamma})=T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. For each
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
, we have
\tilde{v}\in\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
and
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
such that
v=\tilde{v}+\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)
. We call
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)
to be the
horizontal component of
v
.

4.1.1
An explicit description of the map
\theta_{\gamma}
for a connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}

For our future purpose, we will give an explicit description of the map
\theta_{\gamma}:T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
for a connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Let
v\in T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}
. As
s_{*,\gamma}\colon T_{\gamma}X_{1}\rightarrow T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}
is surjective, there exists
w\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
such that
s_{*,\gamma}(w)=v
. Suppose that there exists
w^{\prime}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
with
s_{*,\gamma}(w^{\prime})=s_{*,\gamma}(w)=v
.
For
w,w^{\prime}
we have
w=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)+\widetilde{w}
and
w^{\prime}=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})+\widetilde{w}^{\prime}
with
\widetilde{w},\widetilde{w}^{\prime}\in\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
. Thus,

s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w))=s_{*,\gamma}(w)=s_{*,\gamma}(w^{\prime})=s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})).

Thus,
s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w))=s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime}))
; that is,
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)-\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})\in\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
. As
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\subseteq T_{\gamma}X_{1}
is a vector subspace and
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)-\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
. As
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\bigcap\ker(s_{*,\gamma})=\{0\}
, and
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)-\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}\bigcap\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)-\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})=0
; that is
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})
. So, for
w,w^{\prime}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
with
s_{*,\gamma}(w)=s_{*,\gamma}(w^{\prime})
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w^{\prime})
. We have the description of
s_{*,\gamma}|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}}^{-1}\colon T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
, given by
v\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w)
where
w\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
is such that
s_{*,\gamma}(w)=v
. Thus, the map
\theta_{\gamma}\colon T_{s(\gamma)}X_{0}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma)}X_{0}
is given by
v\mapsto t_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(w))
where
w\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
is such that
s_{*,\gamma}(w)=v
.

4.1.2
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
as a vector bundle over Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. Consider the vector bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
. Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Consider the map
\mu:X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}TX_{0}\rightarrow TX_{0}
, defined as
(\gamma,v)\mapsto\theta_{\gamma}(v)
for each
(\gamma,v)\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}TX_{0}
. This map
\mu
gives an action of
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on
TX_{0}
.

Observe that, for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
, the map
\mu(\gamma,-)=\theta_{\gamma}
, is by definition, a linear map, being composition of linear maps. Thus, with this action of
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on
TX_{0}
, the tangent bundle map
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
is considered as a vector bundle over the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

4.1.3
Comparison of the notion of connections with existing notions in literature

In this section, we will compare our notion of connection on Lie groupoids with the notion of connection on Lie groupoids from the papers
[
1
,
4
]
. The notion of connection on Lie groupoids appear in other works

[
27
,
39
,
64
,
65
]
.

Definition 4.1.14

(
[
1
, Definition
2.8
]
)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid. An
Ehressman connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
is a sub-bundle
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
which is complementary to (kernel of)
s_{*}:TX_{1}\rightarrow TX_{0}
and has the property that
\mathcal{H}_{x}=T_{x}X_{0}
for all
x\in X_{0}
.

2.1

)
.
