\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}},

are cartesian.

Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
as in

Definition

4.1.9
. Consider the set

s^{*}TX_{0}=\{(\gamma,a,v)\in X_{1}\times TX_{0}:s(\gamma)=a,v\in T_{a}X_{0}\}.

This gives a Lie groupoid
[s^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]
with the following description:

•

the source map is given by
(\gamma,v)\mapsto(s(\gamma),v)
,

•

the target map is given by
(\gamma,v)\mapsto(t(\gamma),\theta_{\gamma}(v))
.

The composition, inversion, unit maps are defined similarly. Consider the set

t^{*}TX_{0}=\{(\gamma,a,v)\in X_{1}\times TX_{0}:t(\gamma)=a,v\in T_{a}X_{0}\}.

This gives a Lie groupoid
[t^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]
with the following description:

•

the source map is given by
(\gamma,u)\mapsto(s(\gamma),\theta_{\gamma^{-1}}(v))
,

•

the target map is given by
(\gamma,u)\mapsto(t(\gamma),u)
.

The composition, inversion, unit maps are defined similarly. The map
\theta
gives a morphisms of Lie groupoids
[s^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]\rightarrow[t^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]
(
[
8
, Lemma
4.6
]
).

The compatibility of connection with composition of the Lie groupoid implies that,

s_{*,\gamma_{2}\circ\gamma_{1}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(v)-m_{*,(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2})}(s_{*,\gamma_{2}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(\theta_{\gamma_{1}}(v)),s_{*,\gamma_{1}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(v))\in\ker(t_{*,{\gamma_{2}\circ\gamma_{1}}}),

for each
v\in T_{s(\gamma_{1})}X_{0}
. Suppose that

s_{*,\gamma_{2}\circ\gamma_{1}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(v)-m_{*,(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2})}(s_{*,\gamma_{2}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(\theta_{\gamma_{1}}(v)),s_{*,\gamma_{1}}|_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(v))=0

for each
(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2})\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}X_{1}
and
v\in T_{s(\gamma_{1})}X_{0}
, then,
[\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{0}]
is a subgroupoid of
[TX_{1}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]
. It turns out that, our definition of connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
implies the definition of connection in
[
1
]
. The isomorphism
[s^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]\rightarrow[t^{*}TX_{0}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]
implies that
\mathcal{H}
is a connection in terms of
[
4
]
.

4.2
Atiyah sequence and connection on principal bundle over Lie groupoid

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid, and
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. As mentioned in the introduction, our next aim is to associate a sequence of vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
for the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

The notion of Atiyah sequence and connection on a principal bundle over a manifold is discussed in detail in
Section

2.4
.

For the principal bundle
E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
, we have the Atiyah sequence,

0\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow TX_{0}\rightarrow 0,

of vector bundles over the manifold
X_{0}
. Our aim is to turn this into a short exact sequence of vector bundles over the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.
As mentioned in
Section

4.1.2
, after fixing a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, the tangent bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
can be considered as a vector bundle over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. This gives the tangent bundle
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
a vector bundle structure over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. We expect that this connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
would turn
(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow X_{0}
and
(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow X_{0}
into vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

An action of
\mathbb{X}
on
(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow X_{0}
is given by a map

\mu\colon X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(TE_{G})/G.

For each
\gamma\in X_{1}
with
(\gamma,-)\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(TE_{G})/G
we need a map

\mu_{\gamma}\colon((TE_{G})/G)_{s(\gamma)}\rightarrow((TE_{G})/G)_{t(\gamma)}.

An arbitrary element of
X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(TE_{G})/G
is of the form
(\gamma,[v])
where
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{a}E_{G}
with
\pi(a)=s(\gamma)
. For
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
, we have
t(\gamma)=\pi(\gamma a)
.
That is, for each
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
we need a map

\mu_{\gamma}\colon((TE_{G})/G)_{\pi(a)}\rightarrow((TE_{G})/G)_{\pi(\gamma a)}.

The pull-back diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces TE_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(TE_{G})/G}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces q^{/G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi}

yields following isomoprhism,
((TE_{G})/G)_{\pi(a)}\cong T_{a}E_{G}
and
((TE_{G})/G)_{\pi(\gamma a)}\cong T_{\gamma a}E_{G}
.
That means giving
\mu_{(\gamma,a)}
is same as giving
\mu_{(\gamma,a)}:T_{a}E_{G}\rightarrow T_{\gamma a}E_{G}
.

Recall after
Definition

4.1.1
we have observed
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
is a Lie groupoid, and in fact,
\mu_{(\gamma,a)}
is a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

A principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
can be viewed as a morphism of Lie groupoids

({\rm pr}_{1},\pi):[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]\rightarrow[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}].

We now see that for the differential of the projection map
d({\rm pr}_{1})\colon Ts^{*}E_{G}\rightarrow TX_{1}
, the pull-back
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}=d({\rm pr}_{1})^{-1}(\mathcal{H})
is a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

4.2.1
Pull-back connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]

For
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}=(d({\rm pr}_{1}))^{-1}(\mathcal{H})\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
to form a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, we need

\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}=T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}

(4.2.1)

to hold for each
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
. Here
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}=({\rm pr}_{1})^{-1}_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1})
.
As
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we have

\ker(s_{*,\gamma})\oplus\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}=T_{\gamma}X_{1}

(4.2.2)

for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
.

Let
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
; that is,
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
and
w\in T_{a}E_{G}
such that
s_{*,\gamma}(v)=\pi_{*,a}(w)
.
Suppose that
(v,w)\in\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})\bigcap\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}
. As
(v,w)\in\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})
, we have
w=0
.
Whereas,
(v,w)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})=({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}^{-1}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1})
means
v\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
.
The condition that
s_{*,\gamma}(v)=\pi_{*,a}(w)
and
w=0
implies that
v\in\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
. But,
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is a connection, thus, the condition

v\in\ker(s_{*,\gamma})\bigcap\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
implies that
v=0
.
Thus, we conclude

\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})\bigcap\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}=\{0\}.

Let
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
. As
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}=\ker(s_{*,\gamma})\oplus\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
we have
v=\widetilde{v}+\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)
where
\widetilde{v}
is projection of
v
onto
\ker(s_{*,\gamma})
and
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)
is the projection of
v
onto
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
.
As
({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\widetilde{v},0)=0
, we obtain

(\widetilde{v},0)\in\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)}).

Since
({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
; that is,
(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)\in({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}^{-1}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1})
, we obtain,

(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}.

So, given
(v,w)\in T_{\gamma}\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
, we have

\displaystyle(v,w)=(\widetilde{v},0)+(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)\in\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})+\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G},

(4.2.3)

which along with the condition
\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})\bigcap\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}=\{0\}

imply that

\ker(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)})\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}=T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}.

Explicitly we can write, for each
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}=X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}E_{G}
, we have

\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(w)=t_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,w))

for some
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}
.
In case of
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, we have the target map
t=\mu
.
So, given
w\in T_{a}E_{G}=T_{s(\gamma,a)}E_{G}
, we have

\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(w)=\mu_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)

(4.2.4)

for some
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
with

s_{\gamma}(v)=\pi_{*,a}(w)
. It is easy to see that the above mentioned
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
and the corresponding
\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}\colon T_{s(\gamma,a)}E_{G}\rightarrow T_{t(\gamma,a)}E_{G}
for each
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}

is such that
e_{*,a}(T_{a}E_{G})=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(1_{\pi(a)},a)}s^{*}E_{G}
and that
\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}\circ\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma^{\prime},a^{\prime})}=\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma\circ\gamma^{\prime},a)}
for all composable
(\gamma,a),(\gamma^{\prime},a^{\prime})
in
s^{*}E_{G}
. Thus, the distribution
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}=(d({\rm pr}_{1}))^{-1}(\mathcal{H})\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
defines a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

Lemma 4.2.1
.

If
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is a connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, then, the pull-back
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
is a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. Further, if
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is an integrable connection, then
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
is an integrable connection.

4.2.2
(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow X_{0}
as a vector bundle over Lie groupoid

Now that we have a connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, we can give an action of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on the manifold
(TE_{G})/G
.

Consider the map
X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(TE_{G})/G
given by
(\gamma,[(a,v)])\mapsto[\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)]
. This gives an action of the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
on the manifold
(TE_{G})/G
. With this action, we have the vector bundle
((TE_{G})/G\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

4.2.3
(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow X_{0}
as a vector bundle over the Lie groupoid

The action
X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(TE_{G})/G
mentioned above, restricts to smooth map
X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
, giving the vector bundle

((E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
. To be more precise, we have
\gamma\cdot[(a,A)]=[\gamma\cdot a,A]
for all

(\gamma,[(a,A)])\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
.

Combining the constructions in

Section

4.1.2
,
Section

4.2.2
, and

Section

4.2.3
, we get a short exact sequence,

0\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G\rightarrow(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow TX_{0}\rightarrow 0,

(4.2.5)

of vector bundles over the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Definition 4.2.2
.

Let
G
be a Lie group,
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
a Lie groupoid,
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. The short exact sequence in
Equation

4.2.5
is called the
Atiyah sequence of vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
associated to
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

Definition 4.2.3
.

Let
G
be a Lie group,
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
a Lie groupoid, and
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. A
connection on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
is defined as a splitting of the Atiyah sequence of vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
associated to
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
(
Equation

4.2.5
).

4.3
differential forms on a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection

Let
G
be a Lie group,
M
a smooth manifold, and
\pi:P\rightarrow M
a principal
G
-bundle. We have seen in
Section

2.4
that a connection on
P(M,G)
defined as a splitting
\mathcal{D}
of the Atiyah sequence
(Diagram
2.4.6
) determines a differential
1
-form on
P
, which we called the connection
1
-form associated to
\mathcal{D}
.
In this section, we introduce the notion of a differential form on a Lie groupoid, so that we can associate a differential
1
-form with the splitting.

In literature, there is already a notion of differential forms/ de Rham cohomology on Lie groupoids (
[
40
, Section
3.1
]
). Here we introduce a new notion of a differential form on a Lie groupoid, equipped with a connection. So, we are actually defining a differential form on the pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
.

Definition 4.3.1
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid, and
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Let
\omega:X_{1}\rightarrow\Lambda^{k}T^{*}X_{1}
be a differential form on
X_{1}
. The
horizontal component of
\omega
, denoted by
\mathcal{H}(\omega)
, is a differential
k
-form on
X_{1}
, defined as

\mathcal{H}(\omega)(\gamma)(v_{1},\cdots,v_{k})=\omega(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\cdots,\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{k})),

for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
,
v_{1},\cdots,v_{k}
in
T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. Here,
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)
is the horizontal component of
v
(
Remark

4.1.13
).

Definition 4.3.2

(
[
40
, Definition
5.1.
]
)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid, and
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. A
differential
k
-form of
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
, is a differential
k
-form
\omega
on
X_{0}
, such that
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\omega)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\omega)
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid,
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.
Let
\Omega^{k}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
be the vector space of differential
k
-forms of
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
. Thus, we have a collection of vector spaces
\{\Omega^{k}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\}_{k=0}^{\dim X_{0}}
. Similar to the case of a cochain complex

\Omega^{0}(M)\rightarrow\Omega^{1}(M)\rightarrow\Omega^{2}(M)\cdots,

which we use to define de Rham cohomology of
M
, we would like to construct a cochain complex

\Omega^{0}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\rightarrow\Omega^{1}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\rightarrow\Omega^{2}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\cdots.

The usual exterior derivation operator
d:\Omega^{k}(X_{0})\rightarrow\Omega^{k+1}(X_{0})
do not always preserve the property of “being a differential form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
”. As we will see below, an extra condition on
\mathcal{H}
, of being an integrable connection, ensures that the exterior derivation operator preserve the property of “being a differential form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
”.

The following result was mentioned in
[
11
, Lemma
5.2
]
without proof. In our paper
[
9
]
, we have given a proof. Following is a more detailed version of the proof in
[
9
]
.

Lemma 4.3.3

(
[
11
, Lemma
5.2
]
)
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
an integrable connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. If
\varphi
is a
k
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, then, the exterior derivative
d\varphi
of
\varphi
, when
\varphi
is seen as a
k
-form on the manifold
X_{0}
, is a
k+1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Proof.

We prove for the case
k=1
; that is, when
\varphi
is a
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. The proof works almost verbatim for arbitrary
k
. As
\varphi\colon X_{0}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}T^{*}X_{0}
is a
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we have
\varphi
a
1
-form on
X_{0}
, satisfying the condition
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\varphi)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\varphi)
. That is,
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(v)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(v)
for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. By definition,
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(v)=(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma})(v)
and
\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(v)=(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma})(v)
. Thus, for the
1
-form
\varphi
on the manifold
X_{0}
, we have

(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}v)=(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}v)
for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
.

For such a
1
-form
\varphi
on the manifold
X_{0}
, we prove that, the exterior derivative
d\varphi
, which is a
2
-form on the manifold
X_{0}
, is a
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. For that, we need to prove
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(d\varphi))=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(d\varphi))
as
2
-forms on the manifold
X_{1}
; that is,

\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(d\varphi))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(d\varphi))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})
for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. By definition, we have

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(d\varphi))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})

\displaystyle=s^{*}(d\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=d(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})),

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(d\varphi))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})

\displaystyle=t^{*}(d\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=d(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})).

Assuming
(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}v)=(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}v)
for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
, we prove that
d(s^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=d(t^{*}\varphi)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))

for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
.

For notational convenience, we write
\varphi_{1}=s^{*}\varphi
and
\varphi_{2}=t^{*}\varphi
.

Fix
\gamma\in X_{1}
. Let
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
and consider their horizontal components
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})
. Observe that, for these horizontal vectors
\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}X_{1}
, there exists horizontal vector fields
Z_{1},Z_{2}\colon X_{1}\rightarrow TX_{1}
such that
Z_{1}(\gamma)=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})
and

Z_{2}(\gamma)=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})
. Then, we have

\displaystyle(d\varphi_{1})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=(d\varphi_{1})(\gamma)(Z_{1}(\gamma),Z_{2}(\gamma))=(d\varphi_{1})(Z_{1},Z_{2})(\gamma),

\displaystyle(d\varphi_{2})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=(d\varphi_{2})(\gamma)(Z_{1}(\gamma),Z_{2}(\gamma))=(d\varphi_{2})(Z_{1},Z_{2})(\gamma).

For vector fields
Z_{1},Z_{2}\colon X_{1}\rightarrow TX_{1}
, the exterior derivative
d\varphi_{1}
is given by

(d\varphi_{1})(Z_{1},Z_{2})=Z_{1}\varphi_{1}(Z_{2})-Z_{2}(\varphi_{1}(Z_{1}))-\varphi_{1}([Z_{1},Z_{2}]).

Integrality of
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
implies that, for horizontal vector fields
Y,Y^{\prime}
on
X_{1}
, the Lie bracket
[Y,Y^{\prime}]
is a horizontal vector field on
X_{1}
. As
\varphi_{1}(\widetilde{\gamma})(\mathcal{H}_{\widetilde{\gamma}}(v))=\varphi_{2}(\widetilde{\gamma})(\mathcal{H}_{\widetilde{\gamma}}(v))
for
\widetilde{\gamma}\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\widetilde{\gamma}}X_{1}
, we see that the differential forms
\varphi_{1}
and
\varphi_{2}
agree on horizontal vector fields; in particular, we have

\varphi_{1}(Z_{1})=\varphi_{2}(Z_{1})
,
\varphi_{1}(Z_{2})=\varphi_{2}(Z_{2})
and
\varphi_{1}([Z_{1},Z_{2}])=\varphi_{2}([Z_{1},Z_{2}])
. So, we have

\displaystyle(d\varphi_{1})(Z_{1},Z_{2})

\displaystyle=Z_{1}\varphi_{1}(Z_{2})-Z_{2}(\varphi_{1}(Z_{1}))-\varphi_{1}([Z_{1},Z_{2}])

\displaystyle=Z_{1}\varphi_{2}(Z_{2})-Z_{2}(\varphi_{2}(Z_{1}))-\varphi_{2}([Z_{1},Z_{2}])

\displaystyle=(d\varphi_{2})(Z_{1},Z_{2}).

For
\gamma\in X_{1}
, we have
d\varphi_{1}(\gamma)(Z_{1}(\gamma),Z_{2}(\gamma))=d\varphi_{2}(\gamma)(Z_{1}(\gamma),Z_{2}(\gamma))
and thus

(d\varphi_{1})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=(d\varphi_{2})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})).

Since
\gamma,v_{1},v_{2}
were arbitrary, we have

(d\varphi_{1})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=(d\varphi_{2})(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})),

for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
.
Thus, for a
1
-form
\varphi
on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
with respect to an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
, the condition
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\varphi)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\varphi)
implies that
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}d\varphi)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}d\varphi)
. Thus,
d\varphi
is a
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Using similar arguments, it follows that, for a
k
-form
\varphi
on Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, the exterior derivative
d\varphi
of
\varphi
, is a
k+1
-form on the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.
∎

Now, our aim is to associate a
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
for a connection
\mathcal{D}
on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
. Before we proceed to that, we will present some basic properties related to differential forms on a pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
(
Proposition

4.3.5
,
Proposition

4.3.6
).

Let
f:M\rightarrow N
be a smooth map and
\omega:N\rightarrow\Lambda^{k}T^{*}N
a
k
-form on
N
. Then, we have the notion of the pull-back of
\omega
along
f
, denoted by
f^{*}\omega
, is a
k
-form on
M
, defined as,

(f^{*}\omega)(m)(v_{1},\cdots,v_{k})=\omega(f(m))(f_{*,m}(v_{1}),\cdots,f_{*,m}(v_{k})),

for all
m\in M
,
v_{1},\cdots,v_{k}\in T_{m}M
. In
Proposition

4.3.5
we will see that for a special type of morphism
(F_{1},F_{0}):(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})\rightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
(
Definition

4.3.4
) the pull-back of a
k
-form
\omega
on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
, along the map
F_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Y_{0}
is a
k
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
.

Definition 4.3.4
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}_{X}\subseteq TX_{1}
, and
\mathbb{Y}=[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}_{Y}\subseteq TY_{1}
. We say that a morphism of Lie groupoids
(F_{1},F_{0}):[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]\rightarrow[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
is
compatible with connections
\mathcal{H}_{X},\mathcal{H}_{Y}
, if,

(F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{X}(v))=\mathcal{H}_{Y}((F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(v)),

for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
.

Proposition 4.3.5
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}],\mathbb{Y}=[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
be Lie groupoids equipped with integrable connections
\mathcal{H}_{X}\subseteq TX_{1},\mathcal{H}_{Y}\subseteq TY_{1}
respectively, and
(F_{1},F_{0}):[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]\rightarrow[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
a morphism of Lie groupoids compatible with connections
\mathcal{H}_{X}
and
\mathcal{H}_{Y}
. Let
\omega
be a
k
-form on
Y_{0}
, and
F_{0}^{*}\omega
the pull-back of
\omega
along the map
F_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Y_{0}
. If
\omega
is a
k
-form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
, then,
F_{0}^{*}\omega
is a
k
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
.

Proof.

We will prove this for
k=1
.
The proof for an arbitrary
k
is almost similar.
As
\omega
is a
1
-form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(t_{Y}^{*}\omega)
. Consider the differential form
F_{0}^{*}\omega:X_{0}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}T^{*}X_{0}
. We prove that
F_{0}^{*}\omega
is a
1
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
; that is,
\mathcal{H}_{X}(s_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))=\mathcal{H}_{X}(t_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))
.

Let
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. We have

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{X}(s_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(v)

\displaystyle=(s_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=((F_{0}\circ s_{X})^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=((s_{Y}\circ F_{1})^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=(F_{1}^{*}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\gamma))((F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)))

\displaystyle=(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\gamma))((\mathcal{H}_{F_{1}(\gamma)}((F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(v))))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\gamma))((F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(t_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\gamma))((F_{1})_{*,\gamma}(v))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{X}(t_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(v).

Thus, we have
\mathcal{H}_{X}(s_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(v)=\mathcal{H}_{X}(t_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\gamma)(v)
, for all
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. So,
F_{0}^{*}\omega
is a
1
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
.
∎

We would need a converse of the above result. Suppose that we have the setup as in
Proposition

4.3.5
. One could ask the following question: does
F_{0}^{*}\omega
being a differential form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
imply that
\omega
is a differential form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
. The answer to this question is, yes, if
F_{1}:X_{1}\rightarrow Y_{1}
is a surjective submersion.

Proposition 4.3.6
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}],\mathbb{Y}=[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
be Lie groupoids equipped with integrable connections
\mathcal{H}_{X}\subseteq TX_{1},\mathcal{H}_{Y}\subseteq TY_{1}
respectively, and
(F_{1},F_{0}):[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]\rightarrow[Y_{1}\rightrightarrows Y_{0}]
a morphism of Lie groupoids compatible with connections
\mathcal{H}_{X}
and
\mathcal{H}_{Y}
. Let
\omega
be a
k
-form on
Y_{0}
, and
F_{0}^{*}\omega
the pull-back of
\omega
along the map
F_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Y_{0}
. Suppose further that
F_{1}:X_{1}\rightarrow Y_{1}
is a surjective submersion. If
F_{0}^{*}\omega
is a
k
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
, then,
\omega
is a
k
-form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
.

Proof.

We will prove this for
k=1
.
For an arbitrary
k
, the proof is same. As
F_{0}^{*}\omega
is a
1
-form on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{X}(s_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))=\mathcal{H}_{X}(t_{X}^{*}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))
. We prove that
\omega
is a differential form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
; that is,
\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(t_{Y}^{*}\omega)
.

Let
\gamma\in Y_{1}
, and
v\in T_{\gamma}Y_{1}
. As
F_{1}:X_{1}\rightarrow Y_{1}
is a surjective submersion, for
\gamma
and
v
, there exists
\tilde{\gamma}\in X_{1}
and

\tilde{v}\in T_{\tilde{\gamma}}X_{1}
such that
F_{1}(\tilde{\gamma})=\gamma
and

(F_{1})_{*,\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v})=v
. We have

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(v)=

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\tilde{\gamma}))((F_{1})_{*,\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v}))

\displaystyle=(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\tilde{\gamma}))(\mathcal{H}_{F_{1}(\tilde{\gamma})}((F_{1})_{*,\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v})))

\displaystyle=(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(F_{1}(\tilde{\gamma}))((F_{1})_{*,\tilde{\gamma}}(\mathcal{H}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v})))

\displaystyle=(F_{1}^{*}\circ s_{Y}^{*})(\omega)(\tilde{\gamma})(\mathcal{H}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v}))

\displaystyle=(s_{X}^{*}\circ F_{0}^{*})(\omega)(\tilde{\gamma})(\mathcal{H}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(\tilde{v}))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{X}(s^{*}_{X}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\tilde{\gamma})(\tilde{v})

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{X}(t^{*}_{X}(F_{0}^{*}\omega))(\tilde{\gamma})(\tilde{v})

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(t_{Y}^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(v).

Thus, for each
\gamma\in Y_{1}
and
v\in T_{\gamma}Y_{1}
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{Y}(s_{Y}^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(v)=\mathcal{H}_{Y}(t_{Y}^{*}\omega)(\gamma)(v)
. So,
\omega
is a
1
-form on
(\mathbb{Y},\mathcal{H}_{Y})
.
∎

Some other interesting properties of differential forms on
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}_{X})
will be discussed in later sections.

4.4
1
-form associated to a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
,
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle, and
\mathcal{D}:(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

Viewing
\mathcal{D}
as a morphism of vector bundles over the manifold
X_{0}
, we get a differential form
\omega:E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
, with the property that

\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(v)=(a,\omega(a)(v))
for all
a\in E_{G},v\in T_{a}E_{G}
. Here
\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}:TE_{G}\rightarrow E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g}
is such that
q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}\circ\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}=\mathcal{D}\circ q^{TP}
(
Lemma

2.4.16
).

Considering
\mathcal{D}
as a morphism of vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we have

\mathcal{D}(\gamma\cdot[v])=\gamma\cdot\mathcal{D}([v])

for all
(\gamma,[v])\in X_{1}\times(TE_{G})/G
. We have

\mathcal{D}(\gamma\cdot[v])=\mathcal{D}([\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)])=\mathcal{D}(q^{TP}(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)))=(\mathcal{D}\circ q^{TP})(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v))=q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v))),

and

\gamma\cdot\mathcal{D}([v])=\gamma\cdot(\mathcal{D}(q^{TP}(v)))=\gamma\cdot(\mathcal{D}\circ q^{TP})(v)=\gamma\cdot q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(v))=q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\gamma\cdot\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(v)).

So, we have
q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)))=q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\gamma\cdot\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}(v))
. Rewriting this in terms of differential forms we obtain

q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\gamma a,\omega(\gamma a)(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)))=q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\gamma\cdot(a,\omega(a)(v)))=q^{P\times\mathfrak{g}}(\gamma a,\omega(a)(v)).

Thus, there exists unique
g\in G
such that,

(\gamma a,\omega(\gamma a)(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v)))=(\gamma ag,{\rm{ad}}(g^{-1})\omega(a)(v)).

Comparing the coordinates, and noting that the action of
G
on
E_{G}
is free,
we see that
g=1
. This would then imply that

\omega(\gamma a)(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v))=\omega(a)(v),

(4.4.1)

for all
(\gamma,a)\in X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}E_{G}
and
v\in T_{a}E_{G}
.
The condition in
Equation

4.4.1
implies, that,
\omega
is a
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(with respect to the connection
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}
).

Proposition 4.4.1
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
,
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle, and
\mathcal{D}:(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
. Let
\omega:E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
be the differential
1
-form associated to
\mathcal{D}
. Then,
\omega
is a differential
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(with respect to the connection
\widetilde{H}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
).

Proof.

We prove that
\omega
is a
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
; that is,
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega)=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}\omega)
.

Let
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}=X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}E_{G}
, and
(v,r)\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}\times_{TX_{0}}T_{a}E_{G}
. We have,

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(v,r)

\displaystyle=({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,r))

\displaystyle=({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),r))

\displaystyle=\omega(a)(r),

and

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(v,r)

\displaystyle=(\mu^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,r))

\displaystyle=(\mu^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),r)

\displaystyle=\omega(\gamma a)(\mu_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),r))

\displaystyle=\omega(\gamma a)(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r)).

As
\omega(\gamma a)(\tilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(v))=\omega(a)(v)
(
Equation

4.4.1
), we conclude that,

\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(v,r)=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega)(\gamma,a)(v,r),

for all
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}=X_{1}\times_{X_{0}}E_{G}
, and
(v,r)\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}\times_{TX_{0}}T_{a}E_{G}
. Thus,
\omega
is a differential
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(with respect to the connection
\widetilde{H}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
).
∎

Working out the converse of the above result is straightforward backward calculation.

Proposition 4.4.2
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
,
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. Let
\mathcal{D}:(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
be a morphism of vector bundles over
X_{0}
, which is a connection on
E_{G}(X_{0},G)
, and
\omega:E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
the associated differential
1
-form. If
\omega
is a differential
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(with respect to the connection
\widetilde{H}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
), then
\mathcal{D}
is a morphism of vector bundles over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, thus a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

4.5
2
-form associated to a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
,
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle, and
\mathcal{D}:(TE_{G})/G\rightarrow(E_{G}\times\mathfrak{g})/G
a connection on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
.

Viewing
\mathcal{D}
as a morphism of vector bundles over the manifold
X_{0}
, we get a
\mathfrak{g}
-valued differential
2
-form
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}:X_{0}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}X_{0}
on
X_{0}
, which we called the curvature form associated to the connection
\mathcal{D}
(
Equation

2.4.8
). As in the case of
\omega
, we prove that
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
(with respect to connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
). As mentioned in
Proposition

2.4.17
, we have

\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}=d\omega-[\omega,\omega].

We have already seen that
\omega
is a differential
1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(
Proposition

4.4.1
). As
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
is an integrable connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, the
Lemma

4.2.1
says that,
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq Ts^{*}E_{G}
is an integrable connection on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. The
Lemma

4.3.3
says that
d\omega
is a differential
2
-form on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. If we can prove that
[\omega,\omega]
is also a differential form on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, then, it turns out that
\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
(being a linear combination of differential forms) is a differential form on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.
We need a result to conclude that
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a
2
-form on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
from the observation that
\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a
2
-form on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. As an application of
Proposition

4.3.5
and
Proposition

4.3.6
, we give the following result which implies
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a
2
-form on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
when we know that
\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a
2
-form on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

Lemma 4.5.1
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and

(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq T(s^{*}E_{G})
the pull-back connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. Let
\tau\colon X_{0}\rightarrow\Lambda^{k}T^{*}X_{0}
be a differential
k
-form on the manifold
X_{0}
and
\pi^{*}\tau\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{k}T^{*}E_{G}
the pull-back form on the manifold
E_{G}
along the map
\pi\colon E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
. Then,
\tau
is a differential form on the Lie
groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, if and only if,
\pi^{*}\tau
is a differential
k
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

Proof.

Consider the morphism of Lie groupoids

({\rm pr}_{1},\pi)\colon[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]\rightarrow[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. As
\pi\colon E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
is a surjective submersion, its pull-back
{\rm pr}_{1}\colon s^{*}E_{G}\rightarrow X_{1}
is a surjective submersion. Let
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}
. We have

\displaystyle({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,w))

\displaystyle=({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v),w)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{{\rm pr}_{1}(\gamma,a)}(({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(v,w)).

Thus,
({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,w))=\mathcal{H}_{{\rm pr}_{1}(\gamma,a)}(({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(v,w))
for all
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}
. Thus, the morphism of Lie groupoids
({\rm pr}_{1},\pi)\colon[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]\rightarrow[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
satisfies the following conditions:

1.

the map
{\rm pr}_{1}\colon s^{*}E_{G}\rightarrow X_{1}
is a surjective submersion,

2.

the map
{\rm pr}_{1}\colon s^{*}E_{G}\rightarrow X_{1}
is compatible with the connections
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}
and
\mathcal{H}
in the sense that,
({{\rm pr}}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v,w))=\mathcal{H}_{{\rm pr}_{1}(\gamma,a)}(({\rm pr}_{1})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(v,w))
for all
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v,w)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}s^{*}E_{G}
.

Thus,
\tau
is a differential form on the Lie
groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, if and only if,
\pi^{*}\tau
is a differential
k
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
(
Proposition

4.3.5
and
Proposition

4.3.6
).
∎

Thus, to prove
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a
2
-form on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, all it remains to prove is that
[\omega,\omega]
is a
2
-form on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Let us recall the notion of the Lie bracket of Lie algebra valued differential forms on a manifold. Let
\mathfrak{g}
be a Lie algebra. Let
\omega
and
\eta
be
\mathfrak{g}
-valued differential
k
form and differential
l
-form on a manifold
M
. Then, the Lie bracket
[\omega,\eta]
is a
\mathfrak{g}
-valued differential
k+l
form on the manifold
M
defined as follows:

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} [\omega,\eta](a)&(v_{1},\cdots,v_{k+l})\\
&=\frac{1}{(k+l)!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{k+l}}\text{sgn}(\sigma)[\omega(a)(v_{\sigma(1)},\cdots,v_{\sigma(k)}),\eta(a)(v_{\sigma(k+1)},\cdots,v_{\sigma(k+l)})]\end{aligned}

(4.5.1)

for all
a\in M
and
v_{i}\in T_{a}M
for
1\leq i\leq k+l
.

Lemma 4.5.2
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and

(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle.
Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq T(s^{*}E_{G})
the pullback connection on
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. Let
\mathcal{D}
be a connection on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
and
\omega\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{1}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
the associated connection
1
-form. Then, the Lie bracket
[\omega,\omega]\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
(
Equation

4.5.1
), is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.

Proof.

The differential form
[\omega,\omega]\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
, on the manifold
E_{G}
, is defined as

[\omega,\omega](a)(v_{1},v_{2})=[\omega(a)(v_{1}),\omega(a)(v_{2})],

for all
a\in E_{G}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{a}E_{G}
, where
[\omega(a)(v_{1}),\omega(a)(v_{2})]
is the Lie bracket in
\mathfrak{g}
.

To prove
[\omega,\omega]\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, we prove that
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))
as differential
2
-forms on the manifold
s^{*}E_{G}
; that is,

\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))

for all

(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2})\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
.

For
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2})\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
, observe that

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)

\displaystyle((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))

\displaystyle={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega])(\gamma,a)(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v_{1},r_{1}),\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v_{2},r_{2}))

\displaystyle={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega])(\gamma,a)((\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),r_{1}),(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}),r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega,\omega]({\rm pr}_{2}(\gamma,a))(({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),r_{1}),({\rm pr}_{2})_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}),r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega,\omega](a)(r_{1},r_{2})

\displaystyle=[\omega(a)(r_{1}),\omega(a)(r_{2})],

and that,

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)

\displaystyle((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))

\displaystyle=\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega])(\gamma,a)(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v_{1},r_{1}),\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}_{(\gamma,a)}(v_{2},r_{2}))

\displaystyle=\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega])(\gamma,a)((\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),r_{1}),(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}),r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega,\omega](\mu(\gamma,a))(\mu_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),r_{1}),\mu_{*,(\gamma,a)}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}),r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega,\omega](\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{1}),\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega(\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{1})),\omega(\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{2}))].

From
Equation

4.4.1
we see that
\omega(\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r))=\omega(a)(r)
for all
(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and for all
(v,r)\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
; in particular,

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))

\displaystyle=[\omega(\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{1})),\omega(\gamma a)(\widetilde{\theta}_{(\gamma,a)}(r_{2}))]

\displaystyle=[\omega(a)(r_{1}),\omega(a)(r_{2})]

\displaystyle=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2})).

Thus,

\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2}))=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))(\gamma,a)((v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2})),

for all

(\gamma,a)\in s^{*}E_{G}
and
(v_{1},r_{1}),(v_{2},r_{2})\in T_{(\gamma,a)}(s^{*}E_{G})
. Thus,
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}([\omega,\omega]))=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}([\omega,\omega]))
as a differential
2
-form on the manifold
s^{*}E_{G}
; that is,
[\omega,\omega]\colon E_{G}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}E_{G}
is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.
∎

Lemma 4.5.3
.

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and

(E_{G}\xrightarrow{\pi}X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq T(s^{*}E_{G})
the pull-back connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
.
Let
\mathcal{D}
be a connection on

(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
, and
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
the curvature
2
-form of the connection
\mathcal{D}
on the underlying principal

G
-bundle
E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
. Then
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}

is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

4.6
Chern-Weil map associated to a principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])

Let
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid and

(E_{G}\xrightarrow{\pi}X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
a principal bundle. Let
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
be a connection on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\subseteq T(s^{*}E_{G})
the pull-back connection on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
. Now that we have the notion of curvature form
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
associated to a connection
\mathcal{D}
on principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
, we will introduce the notion of Chern-Weil map.

In
Section

2.4.8
, we have discussed the Chern-Weil map associated to a principal bundle over a manifold. Recall that, for a principal bundle
P(M,G)
, the Chern-Weil map is a morphism of
\mathbb{R}
-algebras
\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{\bullet}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(M;\mathbb{R})
. This is defined by fixing a connection
\omega
on
P(M,G)
and considering the associated curvature form
\Omega:P\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}P
. We will follow a slight variant of the procedure. Instead of using the
2
-form
\Omega
on
P
, we use the
2
-form
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
on
M
associated to a connection
\mathcal{D}
(the splitting associated to the connection
1
-form
\omega
).

Let
f\in\rm{sym}_{k}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}
. Then, we have the differential form
f(\Omega):P\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}P
(
Equation

2.4.9
). We then see that, for this
2
-form
f(\Omega)
on
P
, there exists a unique closed
2k
-form
\widetilde{f(\Omega)}
such that
\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)})=f(\Omega)
. This defined the map
{\rm{sym}}_{k}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}^{2k}(M;\mathbb{R})
as
f\mapsto[\widetilde{f(\Omega)}]
. Using the Atiyah sequence approach, we have associated a
2
-form
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
on
M
, whose pull-back
\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
is the
2
-form on
P
, usually denoted by
\Omega
.

Consider the
2k
-form
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
on
M
. We have

\displaystyle f(\Omega)

\displaystyle=\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)}),

\displaystyle f(\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})

\displaystyle=\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)}),

\displaystyle\pi^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}))

\displaystyle=\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)}).

As
\pi:P\rightarrow M
is a surjective submersion, and
\widetilde{f(\Omega)}
is closed, the condition
\pi^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}))=\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)})
imply that
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
is closed. As
\widetilde{f(\Omega)}
is the unique closed
2k
-form on
M
such that
\pi^{*}(\widetilde{f(\Omega)})=f(\Omega)
, the condition that
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
is closed and
\pi^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}))=f(\Omega)
imply that
\widetilde{f(\Omega)}=f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
. Thus, to define the Chern-Weil map, we can skip one step if we are using the notion of Atiyah sequence approach of connection forms and curvature forms.

4.6.1
de Rham cohomology of the pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})

To define the notion of Chern-Weil map associated to a principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
, we need the notion of de Rham cohomology algebra associated to a pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
, which we will introduce in this section.

For a manifold
M
, after defining the notion of differential forms on
M
, we associate an
\mathbb{R}
-algebra, namely, the de Rham cohomology ring
H^{*}_{{\rm dR}}(M;\mathbb{R})=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\dim(M)}H_{{\rm dR}}^{k}(M;\mathbb{R})
. In this subsection, for a Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
, we associate, what we call, the de Rham cohomology of the pair
(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
, denoted by
H^{*}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
. When there is no confusion regarding the connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
on
\mathbb{X}
, we simply call this the de Rham cohomology of the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Let
\mathcal{DF}^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
denote the vector space of differential
k
-forms on the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}
, with respect to the connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
. For a differential
k
-form
\varphi
on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we have seen that, the exterior derivative
d\varphi
is a differential
k+1
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. This gives a cochain complex,

\cdots\rightarrow\mathcal{DF}^{k-1}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\rightarrow\mathcal{DF}^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\rightarrow\mathcal{DF}^{k+1}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})\rightarrow\cdots.

The
k^{th}
cohomology group of this cochain complex, denoted by
H^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
is called the
k^{th}
-de Rham cohomology of the pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
. Similar to that of the de Rham cohomology ring of a manifold, we can form the
de Rham cohomology ring of the pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
, denoted by
H^{*}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
and defined as

H_{{\rm dR}}^{*}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\dim X_{0}}H^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H}).

(4.6.1)

Remark 4.6.1
.

The paper
[
40
]
defines the de Rham cohomology (groups/ring) of a Lie groupoid in a different way; using the notion of simplicial manifold associated to the Lie groupoid and the corresponding double complex
\Omega^{\bullet}(\Gamma_{\bullet})
.

Example 4.6.2
.

Let
M
be a manifold and
[M\rightrightarrows M]
the associated Lie groupoid. Fix the connection
\mathcal{H}_{m}M=T_{m}M
. Let
\varphi
be a differential
k
-form on the manifold
M
(this
M
is seen as object set of the Lie groupoid
[M\rightrightarrows M]
). As
s,t\colon M\rightarrow M
are identity maps, we have
s^{*}\varphi=\varphi
and
t^{*}\varphi=\varphi
. As
\mathcal{H}=TM
, we have
\mathcal{H}(\varphi)=\varphi
. So, we have
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\varphi)=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\varphi)
for all differential
k
-forms
\varphi
on
M
. Thus, the
k
-th de Rham cohomology group
H^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(M;\mathbb{R})
is equal to the
k
-th de Rham cohomology group of the pair
([M\rightrightarrows M],\mathcal{H})
.

Example 4.6.3
.

Let
G
be a Lie group and
M
a manifold. Let
\mu\colon M\times G\rightarrow M
be an action of the Lie group on the manifold
M
and
[M\times G\rightrightarrows M]
the associated Lie groupoid. Fix the connection
\mathcal{H}_{(m,g)}=T_{m}M
. Then, differential
k
-forms on the Lie groupoid
[M\times G\rightrightarrows M]
are the
G
-invariant differential forms on
M
. So,
H^{k}_{{\rm dR}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})\cong H^{k}(\Omega(M)^{G})
.

4.6.2
Chern-Weil map of the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])

Now that we have the notion of de Rham cohomology algebra associated to a pair
(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
, we can associate the Chern-Weil map as a morphism of
\mathbb{R}
-algebras
\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
.

Lemma 4.6.4

(
[
11
, Theorem
5.3
]
)
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
. Let
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
be a principal bundle. Let
\mathcal{D}
be a connection on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
and
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
the associated curvature
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Then,
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
is a differential
2k
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.

Proof.

We prove this when
k=1
. The general result follows along the same lines of argument. We prove that,
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))
.

Let
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
. We have

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})

\displaystyle=s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}))(\gamma)(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1}),\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))

\displaystyle=(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}))(s(\gamma))(s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))

\displaystyle=f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}(s(\gamma))(s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})))

As
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}\colon X_{0}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}X_{0}
is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
, we see that
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
as differential
2
-forms on the manifold
X_{1}
; that is, for each
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
, we have

\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}(s(\gamma))(s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2}))=\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}(t(\gamma))(t_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),t_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})).

Thus, for
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))\colon X_{1}\rightarrow\Lambda^{2}_{\mathfrak{g}}T^{*}X_{1}
, we have

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})

\displaystyle=f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}(s(\gamma))(s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),s_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})))

\displaystyle=f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}(t(\gamma))(t_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{1})),t_{*,\gamma}(\mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(v_{2})))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2}).

Thus,
\mathcal{H}(s^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})=\mathcal{H}(t^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})))(\gamma)(v_{1},v_{2})
for
\gamma\in X_{1}
and
v_{1},v_{2}\in T_{\gamma}X_{1}
; that is
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
is a differential
2
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. For an arbitrary
k\in\mathbb{N}
and
f\in\text{sym}_{k}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}
, the differential
2k
-form on the manifold
X_{0}
is a differential
2k
-form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
.
∎

Thus, given a connection
\mathcal{D}
on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
, we have associated a morphism of
\mathbb{R}
-algebras

\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
, with
f\in\text{sym}_{k}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}
mapping to
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
. Here,
H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
is the de Rham cohomology of the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}
equipped with the integrable connection
\mathcal{H}
on the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}
.

Now, we see that, this map,
\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
, does not depend on the choice of connection on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
. Let
\mathcal{D}
and
\mathcal{D}^{\prime}
be connections on the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
and
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}}
and
\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}
be the associated curvature
2
-forms on the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Given an element
f\in\text{sym}_{k}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}
, we prove that
[f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})]=[f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}})]\in\mathcal{H}^{2k}(\mathbb{X};\mathcal{H})
; that is, there exists a
2k-1
form
\widetilde{\Phi}
on the Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
; such that
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})-f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}})=d\widetilde{\Phi}
.

Let
\omega,\omega^{\prime}
be the associated connection
1
-forms for connections
\mathcal{D}
and
\mathcal{D}^{\prime}
respectively. Let
\alpha=\omega-\omega^{\prime}
and
\alpha_{t}=\omega^{\prime}+t\alpha
for
0\leq t\leq 1
. Observe that
\alpha_{t}
is a connection
1
-form on the principal bundle
E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
. Let
\Omega_{t}
be the associated curvature
2
-forms. Consider the differential form

\Phi=k\int_{0}^{1}f(\alpha_{t},\Omega_{t},\Omega_{t},\cdots,\Omega_{t})dt

as mentioned in
Equation

2.4.11
. It is known that, this
2k-1
form
\Phi
on
E_{G}
projects uniquely, as
\Phi=\pi^{*}(\widetilde{\Phi})
, to a
2k-1
form on
X_{0}
and that
f(\Omega)-f(\Omega^{\prime})=d\Phi
. So, we have

\displaystyle f(\Omega)-f(\Omega^{\prime})

\displaystyle=d\Phi

\displaystyle f(\pi^{*}\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})-f(\pi^{*}(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}))

\displaystyle=d(\pi^{*}(\widetilde{\Phi}))

\displaystyle\pi^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})-f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}))

\displaystyle=\pi^{*}(d(\widetilde{\Phi}))

As
\pi\colon E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0}
is a surjective submersion, the condition
\pi^{*}(f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})-f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}))=\pi^{*}(d(\widetilde{\Phi}))
implies that
f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})-f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}})=d\widetilde{\Phi}
. To prove that
\widetilde{\Phi}
is a differential form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
it suffices (
Lemma

4.5.1
) to prove that
\Phi
is a differential form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
; that is,
\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\Phi)=\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mu^{*}\Phi)
.
Observe that

\displaystyle{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\Phi

\displaystyle={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\left(k\int_{0}^{1}f(\alpha_{t},\Omega_{t},\Omega_{t},\cdots,\Omega_{t})dt\right)

\displaystyle=\left(k\int_{0}^{1}f({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\alpha_{t}),{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\Omega_{t}),\cdots,{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\Omega_{t}))dt\right)

So, we have

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\Phi)

\displaystyle=k\int_{0}^{1}f(\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\alpha_{t}),\cdots,\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\Omega_{t})))dt.

As
\alpha_{t},\Omega_{t}
are differential forms on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
, we have
\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\alpha_{t})=\mathcal{H}(\mu^{*}\alpha_{t})
and
\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\Omega_{t}))=\mathcal{H}(\mu^{*}(\Omega_{t}))
. So, we have

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\Phi)

\displaystyle=k\int_{0}^{1}f(\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\alpha_{t}),\cdots,\mathcal{H}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}(\Omega_{t})))dt

\displaystyle=k\int_{0}^{1}f(\mathcal{H}(\mu^{*}\alpha_{t}),\cdots,\mathcal{H}(\mu^{*}(\Omega_{t})))dt

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}\left(k\int_{0}^{1}f((\mu^{*}\alpha_{t}),\cdots,(\mu^{*}(\Omega_{t})))dt\right)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}\left(\mu^{*}\left(k\int_{0}^{1}f(\alpha_{t},\cdots,(\Omega_{t}))dt\right)\right)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}(\mu^{*}\Phi).

Thus,
\Phi
is a differential
2k-1
form on the Lie groupoid
[s^{*}E_{G}\rightrightarrows E_{G}]
; which would imply, as mentioned before that
\widetilde{\Phi}
is a differential
2k-1
form on the Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
. Thus, we have the following result:

Lemma 4.6.5
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
. Let
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
be a principal bundle. The map
\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
defined as
f\mapsto f(\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{D}})
for a connection
\mathcal{D}
on
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
does not depend on the connection
\mathcal{D}
.

Definition 4.6.6
.

Let
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
be a Lie groupoid equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
. For a principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
the map
\text{sym}(\mathfrak{g})^{G}\rightarrow H^{*}_{\rm{{\rm dR}}}(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{H})
is called
the Chern-Weil map for the principal bundle
(E_{G}\rightarrow X_{0},[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}])
over a Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}=[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
equipped with an integrable connection
\mathcal{H}\subseteq TX_{1}
.

Chapter 5
Connections on principal bundles over differentiable stacks

In Chapter
4
, we have studied the notion of principal

G
-bundle over a Lie groupoid
\mathbb{X}
for a Lie group
G
. It is a well-known result that, if two Lie groupoids
\mathbb{X}
and
\mathbb{Y}
are Morita equivalent, then the associated categories of principal
G
-bundles over
\mathbb{X}
is equivalent to the category of principal
G
-bundles over
\mathbb{Y}
(
[
40
, Corollary
2.12
]
). This suggest the notion of a principal bundle over a differentiable stack, as a differentiable stack is nothing but a Morita equivalence class of a Lie groupoid (
Lemma

2.3.30
and
Proposition

3.3.4
).

In this chapter, we recall the notion of principal bundles over differentiable stacks and study connections on them.

5.1
Principal bundles over differentiable stacks

In literature, the notion of principal
G
-bundle over a differentiable stack, for a Lie group
G
, appears in different (but equivalent) forms. We will first recall some of these definitions.

Let
G
be a Lie group,
M
a manifold, and
\pi:P\rightarrow M
a principal
G
-bundle. Then, we have an action of the Lie groupoid
[G\rightrightarrows*]
on
P
, which is nothing but the action of
G
on
P
coming from the principal bundle structure. We also have an action of the
Lie groupoid
[M\rightrightarrows M]
on the manifold
P
; which is precisely the map
\pi:P\rightarrow M
. With these actions, the manifold
P
is considered as a
[M\rightrightarrows M]-[G\rightrightarrows*]
-bibundle, as in the following diagram,

\hbox to130.3pt{\vbox to78.46pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 65.14815pt\lower-39.2292pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {}{}{}{{}}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hbox{\hbox{{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {{}{}{{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}}{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{{}{}{{
{}{}}}{
{}{}}

Conversely, suppose that
P
is a
[M\rightrightarrows M]-[G\rightrightarrows*]
-bibundle. The anchor map
\pi:P\rightarrow M
is a principal
G
-bundle. The map
P\rightarrow*
being
[M\rightrightarrows M]
-invariant is not an extra condition, as the map
P\rightarrow*
is trivially a
[M\rightrightarrows M]
-equivariant map. Thus, an
[M\rightrightarrows M]-[G\rightrightarrows*]
-bibundle is same as a principal
G
-bundle. This we have mentioned as Example
2.3.34
. Similarly, for a Lie group
G
, and a Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
a principal
G
-bundle over
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
is same as a
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]-[G\rightrightarrows*]
-bibundle.

We have mentioned in
Section

3.3.2
that, a
\mathcal{G}-\mathcal{H}
-bibundle will assign a morphism of stacks
B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
. Conversely, every morphism of stacks
B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
comes from a
\mathcal{G}-\mathcal{H}
-bibundle (
[
41
, Remark
4.18
]
). Thus, the collection of
\mathcal{G}-\mathcal{H}
-bibundles is in one-one correspondence with the collection of morphisms of stacks
B\mathcal{G}\rightarrow B\mathcal{H}
.
Combining these observations, we can see that the collection of principal
G
-bundles over a Lie groupoid
[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
is in bijective correspondence with morphisms of stacks
B\mathbb{X}\rightarrow B[G\rightrightarrows*]
. Thus, the following definition is a natural choice for a principal
G
-bundle over a differentiable stack.

Definition 5.1.1

(
[
24
, Definition 6.1.]
)
.

Let
G
be a Lie group and
\mathcal{D}
a differentiable stack. A
principal
G
-bundle over
\mathcal{D}
is defined to be a morphism of stacks
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow BG
, where
BG
is the differentiable stack associated to the Lie groupoid
[G\rightrightarrows*]
.

Let
G
be a Lie group,
\mathcal{D}
a differentiable stack, and
\theta:\mathcal{D}\rightarrow BG
a principal
G
-bundle. As
\mathcal{D}
is a differentiable stack, there exists manifold
M
and an atlas
p:\underline{M}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}
. Consider the composition
\underline{M}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\rightarrow BG
. Ignoring
\mathcal{D}
, we see the composition as a morphism of stacks
B([M\rightrightarrows M])\rightarrow BG
. For the reasons mentioned before, the morphism of stacks
B([M\rightrightarrows M])\rightarrow BG
is same as an
[M\rightrightarrows M]\rightarrow[G\rightrightarrows*]
-bibundle; that is a principal
G
-bundle over the manifold
M
. Consider the following
2
-fiber product diagram,

The
2
-isomorphism in the above diagram induces a
2
-isomoprhism
\theta\circ p\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\Rightarrow\theta\circ p\circ{\rm pr}_{2}
. Both of these are functors from
B(M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M)=\underline{M}\times_{\mathcal{D}}\underline{M}\rightarrow BG
. That is, there is an isomorphism of principal
G
-bundles over
M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M
. Further, these bundles satisfy cocycle condition on
M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M
. Thus, given a principal
G
-bundle over
\mathcal{D}
, for an atlas
\underline{M}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}
, we have a principal
G
-bundle over
M
, with an isomorphism of two principal bundles over
M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M
, such that there is a cocycle condition on the manifold
M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M\times_{\mathcal{D}}M
. This motivates the following alternate description of a principal
G
-bundle over a differentiable stack.

Definition 5.1.2

(
[
33
, Definition
2.11
]
)
.

Let
G
be a Lie group, and
\mathcal{D}
a differentiable stack. A
G
-bundle over
\mathcal{D}
is given by a
G
-bundle
\mathcal{P}_{X}\rightarrow X
over the manifold for an atlas
X\rightarrow\mathcal{D}
with an isomorphism of the two pull-backs of
{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\mathcal{P}_{X}\rightarrow{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{P}_{X}
satisfying the cocycle condition on
X\times_{\mathcal{D}}X\times_{\mathcal{D}}X
.

Lemma 5.1.4

(
[
6

]
)
.

are given. If the fibered product

is a submersion, then

is a representable submersion.

Let

be an

-bundle. Then, for a submersion

\mathcal{D}\times_{\mathcal{C}}U

G

5.1.4
, we see that
\pi:\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is a representable submersion.

Definition 5.1.6
.

Let
G
be a Lie group and
\mathcal{C}_{1},\mathcal{C}_{2}
differentiable stacks. A
morphism of principal
G
-bundles from
\mathcal{D}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}_{1}
to
\mathcal{D}_{2}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}_{2}
is given by a pair of morphisms of differentiable stacks
(\Phi:\mathcal{D}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{2},\Psi:\mathcal{C}_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}_{2})

A connection
\nabla
on
\mathcal{D}
is
flat
or
integrable
if it is in addition integrable on each principal
G
-bundle
\mathcal{D}_{u}\rightarrow U
.

Similar to the explanation in
Remark

5.1.5
, the description of connection can be given in terms of atlases with some compatibility conditions.

Let
\nabla
be a connection on
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow U
. Let
u,v
be a pair of atlases of
\mathcal{C}
as in the above diagram.
Let
\omega_{G,u}
be the
\mathfrak{g}
-valued
1
-form on
\mathcal{D}_{u}
(associated to connection
\nabla_{u}
on
U
) and
\omega_{G,v}
the
\mathfrak{g}
-valued
1
-form on
\mathcal{D}_{v}
(associated to connection
\nabla_{v}
on
V
). Consider the
1
-form
{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega_{G,v}
, which is the pull-back of
\omega_{G,v}
of along the smooth map
{\rm pr}_{2}:\varphi^{*}\mathcal{D}_{v}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{v}
. The condition on connection says that, the differential forms
{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega_{G,v},\omega_{G,u}
are related by the isomorphism
\theta_{\alpha}:\mathcal{D}_{u}\rightarrow\varphi^{*}\mathcal{D}_{v}
as

\omega_{G,u}=\theta_{\alpha}^{*}({\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\omega_{G,v}).

5.3
Atiyah sequence associated to principal bundle over differentiable stack

Let
G
be a Lie group, and
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
a principal
G
-bundle. For this principal bundle, we associate a short exact sequence of vector bundles over the stack
\mathcal{C}
. We have done the same for principal bundles over Lie groupoids in
Section

4.2
.

The notion of a tangent stack associated to a differentiable stack is a straightforward generalization of the tangent bundle for a manifold. But, for completeness, we will recall the definition here.

Definition 5.3.1

(Tangent stack
[
33
, Definition/Lemma
4.12
]
)
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a differentiable stack, and
X\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
an atlas of
\mathcal{C}
. Then, we can take the tangent spaces to the groupoid
[X\times_{\mathcal{C}}X\rightrightarrows X]
, namely
[T(X\times_{\mathcal{C}}X)\rightrightarrows TX]
, then the stack associated to
[T(X\times_{\mathcal{C}}X)\rightrightarrows TX]
is independent of choice of atlas
X\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
, and is called
T\mathcal{C}
, the tangent stack to
\mathcal{C}
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a Lie groupoid, and
T\mathcal{C}
be the associated tangent stack. We have seen that a morphism of Lie groupoids induce a morphism of associated differentiable stacks (
Sections

3.3.1
and
3.3.2
). In particular, the morphism of Lie groupoids
[TX_{1}\rightrightarrows TX_{0}]\rightarrow[X_{1}\rightrightarrows X_{0}]
induce a morphism of stacks
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
. As
TX_{1}\rightarrow X_{1}
and
TX_{0}\rightarrow X_{0}
are vector bundles; we can ask if the morphism of stacks
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is a “vector bundle over the stack
\mathcal{C}
”. It turns out that under some special conditions, the morphism of stacks
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is a vector bundle. Firstly, we will recall the definition of a vector bundle over a differentiable stack.

Definition 5.3.2

(vector bundle over differentiable stack
[
30
, Definition
5.1
]
)
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a differentiable stack. A
vector bundle over
\mathcal{C}
is a representable morphism of stacks
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
such that, for every morphism of stacks
f:\underline{U}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
for a manifold
U
, the pull-back
\mathcal{D}\times_{\mathcal{C}}U\rightarrow U
is endowed with structure of a vector bundle. We also require, for every
a:V\rightarrow U
, that the natural isomorphism
\varphi_{a}:(f\circ a)^{*}\mathcal{D}\rightarrow a^{*}(f^{*}\mathcal{D})
is a morphism of vector bundles.

Remark 5.3.3
.

If
\mathcal{C}
is an orbifold, then
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is a vector bundle over
\mathcal{C}
(
[
30
, Lemma
5.2
]
). Moreover, if
\mathcal{C}
is a Deligne-Mumford stack, then
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is a vector bundle over
\mathcal{C}
. However,
T\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
is not a vector bundle over
\mathcal{C}
in general.

From now, we work with principal bundles over Deligne-Mumford stacks.
Similar to the construction of the Atiyah bundle, and adjoint bundle for a principal bundle over a manifold and over a Lie groupoid, we can associate adjoint bundle and Atiyah bundle for a principal bundle over a differentiable stack.

Let
G
be a Lie group, and
\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
a principal
G
-bundle over
\mathcal{C}
. We define the Atiyah bundle

{\rm At}(\mathcal{D})
as

{\rm At}(\mathcal{D})_{u}={\rm At}(\mathcal{D}_{u}),

for any etale morphism
u:U\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
. For a
2
-commutative diagram of the form
